title: Error Handling and Validation
description: Add structured error handling, input validation, and retry patterns to MCP servers in C#.

blocks.text: AI clients handle errors differently from web browsers. A tool failure should include structured information the model can use to recover, such as which field was invalid, what values are allowed, and whether the client should retry.

blocks.title: Recommended error structure
items: **Field** - which parameter or resource caused the failure.
**Retryable** - whether the client should retry or escalate.

blocks.title: Structured tool result error
Never expose stack traces to clients
blocks.text: Log detailed exceptions server-side. Return safe, structured error codes to clients. Stack traces can leak secrets and internal architecture.

items.text: My errors include stable codes and field information
items.hint: Use structured errors instead of random exception messages

items.text: I never return raw exception details to clients
items.hint: Log internally and return sanitized error responses

items.text: My tools are idempotent where possible

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Structured errors help AI clients recover from failures.
Validation should occur before business logic runs.
Never expose secrets or stack traces to MCP clients.
blocks.takeaway: Treat error messages as part of your tool contract. The model reads them to decide what to do next.
